title: Correspondence Standard: Acknowledging Appeals and Grievances Cases and Assigning the Reviewer
content:
Every **Appeals and Grievances** case is acknowledged and placed with a reviewer under this standard.

## Standard

The plan acknowledges each case within the case type's acknowledgment period of the filed date, by the case type's acknowledgment channel, and assigns a reviewer who took no part in the original decision and who has clinical expertise in the member's condition where the case type requires it. Cases the state acknowledges itself go straight to review. All letters are available in accessible formats and in the member's preferred language.

## Status of a case

| From | To | Moved by | What it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| Filed | Acknowledged | The plan's system | The written or oral acknowledgment is sent |
| Acknowledged | Under review | The plan's system | The case is assigned to a reviewer not involved in the original decision |
| Filed | Under review | The plan's system | A case the state acknowledges itself goes straight to review |
| Under review | Resolved | The plan's system | The reviewer resolves the case |
| Filed, acknowledged or under review | Withdrawn | The member | The member withdraws the case |

A case is therefore open while it is filed, acknowledged or under review, and closed once resolved or withdrawn.

## What the records show

- **Acknowledgment.** When a case is acknowledged, its acknowledgment date is recorded and an acknowledgment letter is logged, dated that acknowledgment date. The acknowledgment date is not changed when the case later goes under review.
- **Letters and oral notices.** Every letter or oral notice about a case is logged once per letter and per channel, with the kind of letter, the date it was sent and the delivery channel.

## Points of judgement

- **A case acknowledged by the state.** The plan does not send its own acknowledgment; the case moves from filed straight to under review.
- **Reviewer independence.** A reviewer who took part in the original decision is not assigned to the case.
- **Clinical expertise.** Where the case type requires it, the assigned reviewer has clinical expertise in the member's condition; where the case type does not require it, reviewer independence still applies.
- **Format and language.** Any letter about the case can be provided in an accessible format and in the member's preferred language.
